column2: On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both), from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: “If people were given according to their claims,

men would claim the wealth and the blood of others. But the burden of proof is on the claimant, and the oath is on the one who denies.” A ḥasan hadith, reported by al-Bayhaqī and others in this way; part of it is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs.
This hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās was recorded by al-Bukhārī (4552) and Muslim (1711), and most of it is in the two Ṣaḥīḥs. What is not in them is “the burden of proof is on the claimant”;

but this sentence is established in them from the hadith of al-Ashʿath ibn Qays in al-Bukhārī (4550) and Muslim (138), in a story of his with a cousin of his, in which the Prophet ﷺ said to him: “Your proof, or his oath.”

Ibn Daqīq al-ʿĪd said in his commentary on the Forty: “This hadith is one of the foundations of the rulings and the greatest reference in disputes and litigation; it requires that no one be given judgement in his favour on the strength of his claim alone.”

In it the Prophet ﷺ made clear that if every claimant were granted what he claimed against others, that would lead to claims on people's wealth and lives. But the Prophet ﷺ showed how such disputes between people are to be settled,

namely by requiring proof (bayyinah) from the claimant: anything that makes the truth clear and indicates it, such as witnesses, circumstantial evidence or other things. If he brings the proof, judgement is given on its basis against the defendant;

if there is no proof, the defendant is asked to take an oath. If he swears, he is cleared; if he refuses to swear, judgement is given against him for his refusal and he is bound by what his opponent claimed against him. Al-Nawawī said in his commentary on the Forty: “The burden of proof is on the claimant only

because he claims what is contrary to the apparent state of affairs, and the default is freedom from liability.” Then he mentioned that many cases are excepted in which the claimant's word is accepted without proof, among them a father's claim that he needs [his son to provide for] his marriage;

a legally incompetent person's claim to a longing for marriage, when there is supporting evidence; a woman's claim that her waiting period has ended by menstrual cycles or by giving birth; a child's claim to have reached puberty by a wet dream; and a trustee's claim that the deposit was destroyed or lost through theft and the like.

The claimant is the one seeking, who would be left alone if he kept silent; the defendant is the one sought, who would not be left alone if he kept silent. Ibn al-Mundhir said, as in Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam (2/230):

“The people of knowledge are unanimous that the burden of proof is on the claimant and the oath is on the defendant. He said: The meaning of his words, ‘the burden of proof is on the claimant’, is that by it he becomes entitled to what he claims,
because it is obligatory on him and he is held to it; and the meaning of his words, ‘the oath is on the defendant’, is that by it he is cleared,
because it is obligatory on him and he is held to it in every case.”
Just as the claimant must bring proof for what he claims in worldly matters, so must the claimant bring proof in matters of the Hereafter.
Whoever claims to love Allah and His Messenger ﷺ is truthful in his claim if he follows the Messenger ﷺ, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said:
“Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you and forgive you your sins” [Āl ʿImrān 3:31]. Ibn Kathīr said in his tafsīr of this verse:
“This noble verse judges everyone who claims to love Allah while not being upon the way of Muḥammad: he is in reality a liar,
until he follows the law of Muḥammad and the prophetic religion in all his words and deeds, as is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said:
‘Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our matter, it is rejected.’ That is why He said: ‘Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you’, that is,
you will obtain more than what you sought in loving Him, namely His love for you, which is greater than the first. As one of the wise scholars said:
What matters is not that you love, but that you are loved. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and others of the Salaf said: Some people claimed that they loved Allah, so Allah tested them with this verse.”
The Sharīʿah includes the protection of people's wealth and lives.
The Messenger ﷺ explained the ways by which disputes between litigants are decided.
If the defendant does not admit [the claim], the claimant must establish proof for his claim.
If no proof is established, the defendant is made to swear and is cleared; and if he does not swear, judgement is given against him for his refusal.
